endorsements.quote: Importantly, delineation should include explicit override mechanisms, enabling clinicians to contest AI recommendations without penalty.
Failure visibility mechanisms include confidence scores, uncertainty estimates, and alerts for out-of-distribution inputs ( 4 ).
Authority to modify, suspend, or retire systems when necessary
Rather than proceeding directly to enterprise-wide rollout, DG-TAI requires deployment as a controlled pilot within a limited set of units or facilities.

Applying the DG-TAI framework, the organization begins by establishing a formal governance structure that defines decision rights and accountability across HR, clinical operations, IT, data governance, and compliance.
Processes for monitoring performance, bias, and drift
Differential effects across demographic and socioeconomic groups
Pre-deployment risk assessment and ethical review
Instead, it requires clearly defined ownership, escalation pathways, and authority to intervene when systems underperform or behave unexpectedly.
Effects on clinician workload and cognitive load

unlisted_practices: When AI performance degrades, systems should default to safe modes that preserve human control rather than continuing to generate misleading outputs.
Delineate which tasks are automated, augmented, or reserved exclusively for humans, and keep this role delineation stable and visible.
Design AI systems around the decisions they are intended to influence, explicitly articulating the decision, the responsible user, and the expected relationship between AI output and human judgment.
Apply the same trust, governance, and evaluation principles to operational AI (staffing, scheduling, capacity management) as to clinical AI.
Health systems should build interdisciplinary expertise spanning informatics, clinical leadership, operations, and ethics.
Advance AI from pilot to scale only after predefined trust, equity, and performance thresholds are met, not predictive accuracy alone.
